example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, Stripe, Square and PayPal into one bank account, August. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

chosen.operating-august-statement.pdf: the name of the user's own bank statement file

messages.text: Can you check Stripe, Square and PayPal against our books for August?
Yes. Before I read anything, I need some answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload files?
Which payment apps? I check each one on its own.
Which period? I never assume one.
Does your bookkeeper record each sale, or one entry for each payout?
Does any app hold a reserve or delay payouts?
Optional: what fee rate does your contract set? Then I check the fees against it.

messages.text: Use MosoFin. Stripe, Square and PayPal, all into one bank account. August. One entry for each payout. No reserves. We pay the published rates.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and the company file
messages.summary: The agent can read your books and the three apps. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Your three apps are connected, so I can read both sides. Your chart of accounts has one clearing account for each app: **Stripe Clearing**, **Square Clearing** and **PayPal Clearing**. Are those the right ones?
messages.after: The bank statement never comes through MosoFin. Please attach it, so I can show that the payouts reached the bank.

messages.text: Yes, those are right. Here is the statement.

Here is my plan. I reconcile **Stripe, Square and PayPal** to **Northbrook Trading** for **1 to 31 August**. Sales are recorded **one entry for each payout**. I check each app in its own clearing account, and I compare the fees with the published rates. Shall I start?

messages.label: Read both sides in one batch
messages.summary: 6 reads of your books, the three app reports and your statement. Nothing changed.

messages.text: The three apps charged **$79,500** in August. Each fee matches the published price to the cent:
messages.after: The apps paid **$75,039.95** into your bank. The statement shows the same deposits, so all the money arrived.

messages.text: But one payout is in the wrong clearing account. Your books record a **$1,800 Square payout** against Stripe:
messages.after: Square Clearing has the same $1,800 the other way. Square owed you $20,968.00, but the books record $19,168.00 of Square payouts. In one combined account, the two errors cancel and you see nothing.

messages.text: Stripe sales are recorded **net of fees**. Your books show Stripe sales of **$45,078** and no Stripe fees. That is exactly what Stripe paid out.
messages.after: Profit is the same either way, so nobody noticed. But your sales and your fees are both $1,422 too low. Square and PayPal record their fees, so their sales are right.

messages.text: I propose two entries. Each one points to its evidence:

card.title: Proposed entries
head: Entry
Amount
Evidence
rows: Move the Square payout from Stripe Clearing to Square Clearing
Square payout report and the bank deposit

messages.after: Stripe refunds and chargebacks, $1,500, are also inside Stripe sales. If you keep a refunds account, I can propose a third entry. A person posts these entries. I do not.

messages.text: After the first entry, all three clearing accounts close August at $0. Your workpaper has the summary, the transaction detail, the payout tie-out to your bank statement and the coverage sheet.
messages.after: Do you want the workpaper as an Excel file? And do you want me to save your settings for next month?

messages.text: Done. Here is the Excel file. I saved the clearing account for each app, the posting approach, the payout bank account and the published rates. I never save balances, payouts or customer details.
